analysis: The PR adds one optional diagnostic counter, `cancellationsPartialComplete`, to `DaemonState.Stats` (DaemonStateFile.swift head lines ~133-145). `ProviderLoop+Trust.swift` line 70 populates it from `stats.cancellationsPartialComplete` when the state snapshot is built. The field is optional with a nil default, so older state files still decode, and the snake_case coder strategies are unchanged. The only new data is an aggregate counter of requests that ended early after output was delivered. It carries no prompt content, keys or tokens, and no identifiers (A-001, A-003 and A-008 are not touched). The state file is a local diagnostic that no coordinator-trust or serving decision consumes, per the base source. The write path (`DaemonStateFile.write`, atomic, best-effort) and the read path (schema check) are unchanged. The counter is not exposed on any trust boundary in the supplied diff. The new counter also adds a minor timing or usage signal, but the file is local and same-user, and the existing `requestsServed` and `tokensGenerated` stats already expose comparable data. Open integration questions: where `stats.cancellationsPartialComplete` is defined and incremented (not in the supplied units, so I could not examine it), and whether the coordinator heartbeat or billing logic reads this count. The diff only touches the local diagnostics state, so no regression in the threat model was identified. The field's doc comment, "the coordinator may not pay for them", is a billing-semantics statement; the supplied source does not show it being enforced here.
